name: Raptor Head
summary: At the Crossroads, Raptor Head trophies answer Gazrog’s bounty. Guard payroll vanished from a watchtower, and a wild raptor was caught in the theft.

sections.title: Bounty of the Crossroads
sections.body: A chest of guard payroll was stolen from the Crossroads watchtower, leaving its defenders without their silver. To their disbelief, they caught a wild raptor in the act. Gazrog now offers a bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the Barrens. Bring their severed heads to the outpost, and the predators can be culled before they steal more Horde supplies.

faq.q: Why does Gazrog want raptor heads?
faq.answer: A chest holding silver for the Crossroads guards was stolen from their tower. To everyone’s disbelief, a raptor was caught in the act. Gazrog wants the beasts hunted across the Barrens so they cannot raid the settlement again.

faq.q: Why would wild raptors steal silver?
faq.answer: Gazrog admits he has no idea why wild beasts would want metal coins. Raptors in Kalimdor are known for their unnerving cunning. The theft has left the Crossroads guards embarrassed and eager for retribution.

Heads come from Sunscale raptors roaming the central and southern Barrens, including Sunscale Lashtails, Screechers, and Scytheclaws. Notorious beasts such as Ishamuhale and Takk the Leaper also yield heads.

faq.q: What happens after turning in the heads?
faq.answer: After Gazrog receives twelve heads and the raptor menace is thinned, attention turns to finding where the stolen silver shipment was taken.

angles.text: The Crossroads is the heart of Horde travel in central Kalimdor. Clearing the thieving predators helps secure the garrison’s supplies and payroll.
Tracking Sunscale raptors across the Barrens’ dry scrub tests your skill against some of the savannah’s most aggressive and cunning pack hunters.
